messages:
Nadia K.: Heads up team: rented a van for offsite, company card covered rental but the agency kept the damage deposit because of a small scuff on the rear bumper. They issued a damage charge \u20ac150 two weeks later to the card. Also got a parking ticket while parked overnight (local municipal fine) that I paid personally \u20ac45 because it arrived to my home address. What's reimbursable and how to document the deposit/damage vs the ticket? cc @people-ops
Maya (People Ops): Short: rental damage (if valid and charged to company card) is an allowable business expense. If the charge hit the company card already, Finance will process. If you paid personally for a fine, municipal traffic fines are NOT reimbursable under policy. But split scenarios and security deposit refunds have nuancesdetails below.
Ben (Finance): Add: for the \u20ac150 damage charge on the company card we need the agency invoice/repair estimate showing the damage, date, VIN or booking ref. If the agency withheld deposit and then charged the card, attach the rental agreement and the charge notice. For the \u20ac45 parking ticket you paid personally: policy excludes fines (parking, speeding, toll violations) from reimbursement. If you disagree with the fine, fight it with the municipality; Finance won't reimburse adjudicated fines.
Oliver R.: Follow-up: the agency only provided a photo of the scuff and a short note; no formal invoice. They emailed: "Deposit retained - minor scratch, \u20ac150". Is that enough? They said they can issue an invoice on request but slow.
Maya (People Ops): For charges > $75 we need corroborating documentation. Email + photo is ok as an interim attachment, but please request a formal invoice. If they won't provide one, we can escalate but Finance may request manager approval and additional attestation. Attach the original rental contract showing the deposit amount and the booking ref.
Nadia K.: For the \u20ac45 ticket I paid with my card because it arrived to me. I can upload the municipality notice and my card statement line. Any chance Finance will make an exception?
Ben (Finance): We can't reimburse statutory fines. Exception path: only if the charge was actually a toll/parking fee incorrectly labeled as a fine (e.g., private parking operator vs municipal fine). If you can show it's a private operator fee (contractor invoice) rather than a legal fine, we can reimburse as a business parking expense. Otherwise policy is firm.
Maya (People Ops): Practical steps: 1) Submit rental expense with the agency email+photo, rental agreement, and booking ref. Tag expense "rental damage". 2) Ask agency for invoice; if not forthcoming in 7 days, escalate to People Ops and include manager sign-off. 3) Submit the parking ticket as "non-reimbursable" in the system with attachments so we have a record (switch the reimbursement amount to 0). If it's actually a private parking charge, re-submit as reimbursable with vendor invoice.
ExpenseBot: :receipt: Evidence checklist for damage/retention: - rental agreement + booking ref - charge notice or invoice from rental agency - photos of damage or vehicle - company card transaction line (if charged) - manager attestation if invoice not available and amount > $75. Missing receipt thresholds still apply for other expenses.
Oliver R.: Suppose the agency charged the company card and then refunded a portion later (deposit partially returned). How do we reflect the refund in expenses?
Ben (Finance): For company-card refunds we reconcile automatically on the card feed. If the charge was originally posted to an expense, Finance will apply the refund against the same merchant and amount; no action usually needed. If you had submitted an expense for the original deposit (unlikely on company card), we recommend adding a comment with the refund date/amount. If you (or a teammate) paid personally and later got refunded by the agency, submit a negative expense or attach the refund evidence so we net it properly.
Nadia K.: Also one teammate (Sam) paid for an emergency towing fee \u20ac85 because we were stuck and didn't want to delay the offsite. He requests reimbursement. Is towing treated like a normal transport expense?
Maya (People Ops): Emergency towing for business travel is reimbursable as an operational transport expense. Attach the towing invoice or receipt. If Sam paid personally, upload his receipt + card statement line and mark "emergency towing - offsite". If Sam didn't get a proper receipt, amounts > $75 need manager sign-off and Finance must review.
Ben (Finance): For the towing \u20ac85: acceptable if it looks like a vendor invoice (tow company name, date, amount). If Sam only has a handwritten receipt, we'll need manager approval before reimbursement.
ExpenseBot: :receipt: Missing receipt policy recap: - <= $25: Lost-Receipt Form allowed - $25-75: Lost-Receipt Form + manager approval - > $75: original vendor invoice required (exceptions reviewed by Finance)
Maya (People Ops): Quick template for rental damage submission (paste into description field):
```
Expense: Van rental damage charge
Booking ref: VAN-2026-03-21-99
Original payer: Company card (last4 1234)
Charge amount: 150.00 EUR
Attachments: rental agreement, agency email + photo of damage, company card transaction
Notes: requested formal invoice on 2026-03-25; attaching manager attestation in case invoice delayed
```
Nadia K.: Got it 44d I'll request the formal invoice and submit everything. I'll also upload the municipal notice for the ticket as a non-reimbursable record. Thanks!
Oliver R.: Saved the template. Thanks both. :thumbsup:
